> Kimi-K3 on gfx950 merge queue (all drafts; they land one at a time in this order): 1 #44978 verify argmax + tuned bf16 rows · 2 #44979 MLA prefill · 3 #44980 streaming AttnRes · 4 #44981 MoE prefill · 5 #44982 KDA · 6 #44983 MLA decode prep · 7 #44984 MLA decode epilogue · 8 #44985 LL column tail · 9 #44986 fused all-reduce read · 10 #44987 fused route sort · 11 #44988 split MoE front + bank partials · 12 #44989 MLA q-norm + q_b. Replaces #44547-#44553.

## Motivation

Kimi-K3 prefill on gfx950 leaves three MoE-side costs: the A8W4 experts quantize activations to MXFP8 even where
aiter's MXFP4 x MXFP4 kernels are faster, the merged MoE front GEMM is followed by a separate SiTU kernel for the
shared experts, and every rank runs the latent tail (norm, up-projection, adds) and the FFN-side AttnRes read on all
rows of 4K-8K-token chunks after the all-reduce.

## Modifications

Gated on gfx950.

- SiTU MXFP4 MoE calls of at least `SGLANG_ROCM_K3_PREFILL_MOE_A4W4_MIN_TOKENS` (1025) tokens quantize activations to
  MXFP4 and run aiter's a4w4 kernels on the gate/up-interleaved a8w4 weights (`gate_mode=INTERLEAVE`), only for padded
  sizes whose aiter config resolves to the mxmoe stage 1, the one that honors that layout (`mxfp4.py` records the
  interleaving on the quant info).
- `kimi_k3_front_situ`: at the prefill sizes where it beats the tuned GEMM + SiTU (129-160, 193-320, 1152-1280
  tokens), the merged front runs as one Triton GEMM whose gated tiles pair gate row j with up row 768 + j and write
  SiTU(gate) * up (`SGLANG_ROCM_K3_FRONT_SITU`); configs are compiled at weight-merge time.
- Row-sharded tails for batches of at least `SGLANG_ROCM_K3_ROW_SHARDED_TAIL_MIN_TOKENS` (4096): the MoE reduce-
  scatters its [latent | shared] partials by rows, runs norm + up-projection + shared + residual add on this rank's
  1/8 of the rows and all-gathers the stream; with `SGLANG_ROCM_K3_ROW_SHARDED_ATTN_READ` the attention output's sum,
  the residual add and the FFN read also run on the shard (`AttnBankState.ffn_row_shards`), leaving the residual
  there for the tail. `SGLANG_ROCM_K3_ROW_SHARDED_ATTN_MIN_TOKENS` raises the attention side's threshold separately.

Compared with #44553, this PR no longer stacks on the TP8 collectives and MoE decode changes: it uses none
of their code (the stack was only textual). `_row_sharded_tail_eligible` also drops its clause about the token range
of #44985's column tail, which `0 < min_tokens <= num_tokens` already implied.

| New env var | Default |
|---|---|
| `SGLANG_ROCM_K3_PREFILL_MOE_A4W4_MIN_TOKENS` | 1025 |
| `SGLANG_ROCM_K3_FRONT_SITU` | on |
| `SGLANG_ROCM_K3_ROW_SHARDED_TAIL_MIN_TOKENS` | 4096 |
| `SGLANG_ROCM_K3_ROW_SHARDED_ATTN_READ` | on |
| `SGLANG_ROCM_K3_ROW_SHARDED_ATTN_MIN_TOKENS` | 0 (with the tail) |

## Accuracy Tests

**Setup for every number below:** 8x MI350X (gfx950, 1000 W), Kimi-K3 (MXFP4 MoE, bf16 attention) at TP8 with EAGLE3
(topk 1, 3 steps, 4 draft tokens), FP8 KV cache, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, aiter's K3 FlyDSL kernels
(`AITER_SITUV2_A8W4=1 AITER_FLYDSL_FORCE=1 SGLANG_AITER_K3_OPT=1`), CUDA graphs for bs 1/2/4/8/16, and an aiter bf16 GEMM table with K3 rows re-tuned on this pod with HBM-resident weights
(`AITER_CONFIG_GEMM_BF16`; not part of this PR, it belongs in aiter's model configs). EAGLE3 on K3 needs the
aux-capture commit of #43599, applied locally for these runs. Microbenchmarks rotate their weights through HBM.
Per-feature numbers were measured on the integration branch of this series as each piece landed (Oct 13-14,
earlier `main`). All branches of the series are on `main` 4eb606b2ae (2026-10-17); the kernel tests below ran on this
branch, and the end-to-end checkpoints on that `main` plus the queue up to each slot.

- GSM8K 400: a4w4 prefill 0.9825 / accept 3.619; row-sharded tails (both sides, >= 4096) 0.9875 / 3.621; with the
  40 / 56-token opt-in thresholds 0.9875. End to end: see below.
- `test_kimi_k3_moe_a4w4.py` (new): from the default threshold aiter's config resolves to the interleave-capable
  stage 1 and the a4w4 output tracks a8w4 (cosine > 0.95; a misread gate/up layout gives ~0.004).
- `test_kimi_k3_front_situ.py` (new): the fused front against an fp32 GEMM followed by SiTU on its bf16 output.
- On MI350X, these two with the existing layer-boundary tests `test_kimi_k3_stage_kernels.py` and
  `test_attn_bank_residual_ops.py` (this PR changes `attn_bank.py`): 11 passed, 7 failed (22 subtests passed).
  All 7 failures are in `test/registered/unit/layer_boundary/test_attn_bank_residual_ops.py`, which fails the same
  7 tests on unmodified `main` on this pod (`'_Norm' object has no attribute 'weight'`), unchanged by this PR.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

- a4w4 vs a8w4 per MoE call (K3 TP8): 0.84-0.89x at 1025-2048 tokens, 0.77x at 4096, 0.85x at 8192; uncached 50K
  prefill 3.70 -> 3.60 s.
- Front SiTU vs tuned GEMM + SiTU (median of alternating runs): 144 tokens -31%, 160 -16%, 208-320 -6..-31%,
  1152-1280 -2..-7.5%; in-server extend TTFT -0.4..-2%.
- Row-sharded tails (8K rows): bank read 477 -> 56 us and up-projection 387 -> 55 us on 1K rows, RCCL RS + AG 652 vs
  INT8 quick all-reduce 498 us; uncached 50K prefill 3.47 -> 3.40 s with both sides, agentic turn TTFT neutral.
  Below ~4K tokens RCCL's fixed cost outweighs it (1.9K-token turn +2.5%), hence the default.

and GSM8K 200, EAGLE3 as above, measured 2026-10-17. These runs and the previous integration below also set `SGLANG_AITER_MLA_AUTO_KV_SPLITS=1 SGLANG_AITER_MLA_MAX_SPLITS_PER_BATCH=128 SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_KDA_VERIFY=1 AITER_MLA_REDUCE_FLYDSL=1`. In bold: the first checkpoint that includes this PR.

|---|---|---|---|
| **slot 5** | **#44978, #44979, #44980, #44981, #44982** | **21.6 ms\*** | **0.995** |
| slot 7 | #44983, #44984 | 19.4 ms | 0.990 |
| slot 9 | #44985, #44986 | 18.6 ms | 0.990 |
| slot 10 | #44987, #41867, #41848 | 16.7 ms | 0.985 |
| slot 11 | #44988 | 15.7 ms | 0.990 |
| slot 12 | #44989 | 15.6 ms | 0.990 |

\* The second of two runs; the first, right after start-up, measured 25.6 ms. The other rows average two runs.

The whole series, from the previous integration: the seven earlier drafts (#44547-#44553) merged on `main` b67785153a (this series'
code plus the two opt-in paths it drops, both off by default), with #43599's aux capture, #41867 and #41848; agentic
replay of lightseekorg/agentic-dataset SWE-smith conversations (multi-turn, ~50K-token cached prefixes, 500 output
tokens, greedy), EAGLE3 as above. TokenSpeed (7e2f1deb, same pod, same workload) for reference.

agentic turn TTFT (50K cached + 1.9K new tokens) 230-248 ms; uncached 50K-token prefill 3.27 s. The slot-12

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,190 @@
+"""Kimi-K3 latent-MoE input step in one Triton GEMM with the shared experts' SiTU in its epilogue.
+
+One launch over the merged front weight [shared gate | shared up | router | latent down] (rows).
+A gated tile pairs gate row j with up row N_HALF + j in adjacent columns, so it streams the same
+weight bytes as any other tile and writes SiTU(gate) * up; the rest write router logits and the
+latent input. Replaces the merged-front GEMM followed by a separate SiTU kernel for the prefill
+batch sizes covered() admits.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import torch
+import triton
+import triton.language as tl
+
+# (first, last tokens, (BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N, BLOCK_K, GROUP_M, num_warps, num_stages, waves_per_eu)):
+# the sizes where it beats the tuned merged-front GEMM + SiTU kernel on MI350X, each with the
+# fastest config of a sweep; at the GEMM's tuned sizes and between these, the GEMM wins.
+_RANGES = (
+    (129, 160, (32, 128, 128, 8, 4, 3, 4)),
+    (193, 256, (128, 64, 128, 8, 4, 3, 1)),
+    (257, 320, (64, 128, 128, 8, 4, 3, 2)),
+    (1152, 1280, (256, 128, 64, 8, 8, 3, 1)),
+)
+
+
+def covered(num_tokens: int) -> bool:
+    return any(first <= num_tokens <= last for first, last, _ in _RANGES)
+
+
+def _config(num_tokens: int):
+    for first, last, config in _RANGES:
+        if first <= num_tokens <= last:
+            return config
+    raise ValueError(f"no front SiTU config for {num_tokens} tokens")
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _tanh(x):
+    return 2.0 / (1.0 + tl.exp(-2.0 * x)) - 1.0
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _remap_xcd(pid, num_pids, NUM_XCDS: tl.constexpr):
+    # Hardware deals pids round-robin over the XCDs; give each XCD (one L2) a run of
+    # consecutive pids, so the programs that share a weight panel share its L2.
+    pids_per_xcd = (num_pids + NUM_XCDS - 1) // NUM_XCDS
+    tall_xcds = num_pids % NUM_XCDS
+    tall_xcds = tl.where(tall_xcds == 0, NUM_XCDS, tall_xcds)
+    xcd = pid % NUM_XCDS
+    local_pid = pid // NUM_XCDS
+    return tl.where(

+"""The gfx950 Kimi-K3 MoE front GEMM with a SiTU epilogue against GEMM then SiTU."""
+
+import unittest
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.utils import is_gfx95_supported
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_amd_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+# backend-specific: the fused front is tuned for and selected on gfx950 only.
+register_amd_ci(est_time=15, suite="stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x")
+
+# Kimi-K3 TP8 merged MoE front rows: shared [gate 768 | up 768], router 896, latent 3584.
+GATE_UP, EXPERTS, LATENT, HIDDEN = 1536, 896, 3584, 7168
+BETA, LINEAR_BETA = 4.0, 25.0
+
+
+def _situ(gate_up: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    gate, up = gate_up.float().chunk(2, dim=-1)
+    gate = BETA * torch.tanh(gate / BETA) * torch.sigmoid(gate)
+    return gate * LINEAR_BETA * torch.tanh(up / LINEAR_BETA)
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(is_gfx95_supported(), "gfx950 fused MoE front")
+class TestKimiK3FrontSitu(CustomTestCase):
+    @torch.inference_mode()
+    def test_matches_gemm_then_situ(self):
+        """The fused front pairs gate row j with up row 768 + j and splits the
+        rest into router logits and latent: within one bf16 rounding of an fp32
+        GEMM followed by SiTU on its bf16 output."""
+        from sglang.kernels.ops.gemm.kimi_k3_front_situ import front_situ
+
+        g = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(0)
+        weight = (
+            torch.randn(GATE_UP + EXPERTS + LATENT, HIDDEN, generator=g, device="cuda")
+            * 0.02
+        ).bfloat16()
+        for rows in (144, 300, 1200):
+            x = torch.randn(rows, HIDDEN, generator=g, device="cuda").bfloat16()
+            full = (x.float() @ weight.float().t()).bfloat16()
+            act, rest = front_situ(x, weight, GATE_UP, BETA, LINEAR_BETA)
+            for name, got, want in (
+                ("situ", act, _situ(full[:, :GATE_UP])),
+                ("router|latent", rest, full[:, GATE_UP:]),
+            ):

+                    want = want.float()
